avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Cefazolin may cause hyperkalemia; combined potassium supplementation increases risk of dangerous serum levels
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid potassium supplementation unless specifically prescribed; monitor serum potassium levels

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen, indomethacin)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and may impair cefazolin clearance; increased nephrotoxicity and hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Use alternative pain relief (acetaminophen); if NSAIDs necessary, use lowest dose for shortest duration with renal monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Probenecid
caution_supplements.mechanism: Probenecid inhibits renal tubular secretion of cefazolin, increasing drug levels and duration
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for cefazolin toxicity signs; dose adjustment may be needed if co-administered

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May chelate with cefazolin in GI tract, potentially reducing absorption if oral formulation used
caution_supplements.action: Separate administration by 2+ hours if oral cefazolin is used

caution_foods.name: High potassium foods (bananas, oranges, spinach, nuts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Cefazolin can cause mild hyperkalemia; excessive dietary potassium may contribute to elevated serum levels in susceptible patients
caution_foods.action: Consume in moderation; particularly important for patients with renal impairment or baseline hyperkalemia

monitoring_notes: Cefazolin is minimally metabolized and primarily renounced; monitor renal function (creatinine clearance, BUN) especially in elderly or renally impaired patients. Watch for signs of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations) and allergic reactions, particularly in patients with penicillin/cephalosporin cross-reactivity history.
